html:
The Tjupan are an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland Goldfields and Mid West of Western Australia, on the western edge of the desert. The map shows them as Tjupany from 1600 to 1815. Their language is one of the Wati languages of the Pama-Nyungan family, sometimes counted as a dialect of the Western Desert language of the Western Desert cultural bloc.

Their neighbours were the Koara to the west, the Nana to the east and the Wawula to the north. A nearby people, the Pini, spoke a language close to Tjupan that was never written down. Gold mining towns sprang up across this country in the 1890s.
